findings.failure_scenario: A held commit that breaks fresh-clone install or setup turns cold-setup red by status inside a green run (continue-on-error); last-ci, land.mjs and check-ci-evidence read only the run conclusion, so the next batch lands over it unless someone opens the job by hand.

findings.evidence: UPSTREAM.sha256 comes from src/icons.json's sourceSha256 and revision is a literal; no test compares them with specs/import/corpus/manifest.json (iconify-lucide commit db4c0e1c..., iconify entry sha256 bcf5691c...) or hashes the corpus file; pack.test.ts compares pack/ only with the exported source built from icons.json. ADR-0050: 'The checked-in first-party source manifest links those hashes to actual input files and license/notice evidence; the gate verifies those files.' packs/icons-lucide/package.json declares "license": "MIT" although dist/index.js bundles the ISC AND MIT artwork (pack index license 'ISC AND MIT'); ADR-0050: 'A wrapper package's MIT declaration cannot replace the rights and notices of the artwork it contains.'
findings.failure_scenario: A hand edit of icons.json (a modified path, or an icon added from outside the pinned collection) or a re-pin of the corpus without regenerating keeps every test green while the credits claim the old pinned source; npm metadata and license scanners downstream see only MIT.
findings.recommendation: Add a node test in packs/icons-lucide asserting sourceSha256 equals the manifest's iconify-lucide sha256 and the corpus file's hash, the revision equals the manifest commit, the notices equal specs/import/corpus/licenses/lucide.txt split as lucide.mjs does, and every icon name exists in the pinned collection; set package.json license to 'MIT AND ISC' (check-licenses still passes, both allowlisted) or record why MIT is right in an argue line.
